title: Realm 1: The Spark of the Web
description: Master console output, variables with let and const, and template strings.

lessons.title: 1. Hello, JavaScript!
lessons.concept:
### Welcome to JavaScript! ⚡
JavaScript is the programming language that powers every interactive website on the planet.

In JavaScript, we use **`console.log()`** to print messages to the console.

```javascript
console.log("Hello, Web Hero!");
```

Unlike Python, JavaScript uses parentheses `()` and usually ends lines with a semicolon `;`.
lessons.task: Write a `console.log()` command that prints: `Welcome to JavaScript Hero!` exactly as shown.
lessons.starterCode:
// Write your code below and click Run Spell:
console.log("Hello, World!");
hints: Change 'Hello, World!' to 'Welcome to JavaScript Hero!'

lessons.title: 2. Variables: let vs const
lessons.task: Declare a variable `let heroName = "Volt";` and a variable `let power = 900;`. Print both using `console.log()`.

lessons.task: Check if `let mana = 50;` is greater than or equal to 30. If so, print `Spell ready!`. Otherwise print `Need mana.`.

lessons.title: 5. Arrays & Push / Pop
lessons.concept:
### JavaScript Arrays `[]`
An array is a list of items:

```javascript
const inventory = ["Sword", "Shield"];
inventory.push("Magic Wand"); // Adds to end
console.log(inventory[0]); // 'Sword'
console.log(inventory.length); // 3
```

lessons.title: 6. Arrow Functions
lessons.concept:
### Modern Arrow Functions `=>`
Arrow functions are clean and concise ways to write functions:

```javascript
const double = (n) => n * 2;
console.log(double(5)); // 10
```
lessons.task: Create an arrow function named `add` that takes `(a, b)` and returns `a + b`. Call `add(10, 20)` and print the result.
lessons.solution:
const add = (a, b) => a + b;
console.log(add(10, 20));
